result.note: Tests the developer, cell line and dosing schedule of India's first indigenous African Swine Fever vaccine.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) unveiled India's first indigenous vaccine against African Swine Fever. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It was developed by ICAR's National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal.
It is produced using the MA-104 cell line.
It is recommended for pigs above eight weeks, with a booster dose after 28 days.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The third statement is wrong because the vaccine is given to pigs above eight weeks as a single dose with a booster after 14 days, not 28. African Swine Fever has spread across India since 2020.
questions.source: Built by ICAR's National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD) in Bhopal, the vaccine uses the widely available MA-104 cell line and is recommended for pigs above eight weeks as a single dose with a booster after 14 days.
